title: AREA FIREWORKS SHOWS
full_story:
Fireworks will be featured at area communities starting tonight.

The festivities begin tonight in Fairfield with Freedom Fest at Southwest Park from 5 to 10 pm.  The event will feature inflatables, children’s games, a foam pit, putt-putt golf, food trucks and craft vendors, live music, and fireworks at dusk.  Country artist Noah Atwood is scheduled to perform.  Admission is free.

The Village of Cisne will kick off its Independence Day celebration tomorrow, with an evening of food, live entertainment, and fireworks.  Food trucks will open at 5 pm in the back parking lot of Cisne High School.  Vendors scheduled to participate include Lil Buddies Snack Trailer, The Fair Lady, and Krazy Sweet Treats.  TrustBank will sponsor the first 100 snow cones for attendees.  The celebration will conclude with a fireworks display at dusk at the high school ball diamond.

Flora’s fireworks celebration begins Saturday at 10 am at Charley Brown Park.

title: SBDC PROGRAMS ON BUSINESS
full_story:
The SBDC at IECC is presenting a lender Forum on July 14th from 9 to Noon in the OCC Banquet Room.

Presenters will include SBA staff, 504 corporations, SBDC representatives, Illinois Advantage Representatives, the state Treasurers Office, and microlenders.  Topics will include SOP Changes, updated lender match info, and upcoming SBA initiatives and training opportunities.

Then from 1 to 3 pm the SBDC at IECC will present a session on Funding opportunities for Businesses in the same room.

Speakers will include Mark Lambird talking about TIF and Enterprise Zone Fund, The Greater Wabash Regional Planning Commission, Advantage Illinois, the SBA and Trustbank.

For more information or to sign up for the Workshop call Michelle Brooks at 618-562-3744 or visit the iecc.edu/sbdc website.

The programs are funded in part through a cooperative agreement with the US SBA, the Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity and the Illinois Eastern Community College.

title: FARM BUREAU ANNUAL MEETING
full_story:

title: FCC BASEBALL CAMP
full_story:
Frontier Community College Baseball will host Summer Youth Camps this month for players interested in learning and improving their baseball skills.

The camps will be divided into two age groups.  Kids Camp 1, for ages 5 through 9, will be held July 13th and 14th from 9 am to noon each day.  Kids Camp 2, for ages 10 through 13, will be held July 15th and 16th from 9 am to noon each day.

Each camp will focus on skill development in all areas of the sport, including throwing, hitting, catching, and base running.  The camps are designed to help young players build fundamentals, gain confidence, and enjoy the game of baseball in a fun and encouraging environment.

The cost to attend is $60 per camper.  All camps will be held at FNB Field on the campus of Frontier Community College, weather permitting.

Participants may register up to the day of the event; however, campers are asked to be registered by Monday, July 6th.

To register, call FCC Student Services at 618-847-9135 or visit FCC Student Services on campus.  For questions or more information, contact Bobcats Head Baseball Coach Matt McCue at [email protected] or 618-847-9271.

title: OSLAD GRANT APPLICATIONS
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Natural Resources (IDNR) is accepting applications for Open Space Land Acquisition and Development, or OSLAD, grants through August 31st.

A total of $37.5 million is available for this round of OSLAD grants.  IDNR will again provide funding to cover 100% of eligible projects in economically distressed communities.  In the most recent round of OSLAD awards announced in January, 20th underserved locations received grants for local park projects.

In addition, communities whose parks need to be rebuilt as a result of storm damage are encouraged to apply for OSLAD grants.  Under state administrative rules, entities recovering from storm damage can apply as physically distressed communities, allowing them to only need 10% matching funds.

OSLAD is a matching grant program that offers state-financed funding assistance to local governmental agencies for the acquisition and/or development of land for public parks and outdoor recreation areas.  Since it was established by the Illinois General Assembly in 1986, OSLAD has awarded more than $675 million for local park projects throughout Illinois.

Applications must be submitted by 5 pm on Monday, August 31st through the Amplifund portal website.  Before applying for a grant, entities must be registered and current in the state’s Grant Accountability and Transparency Act grantee portal.

For more information, visit the OSLAD website or call 217-782-7481.

title: SUMMER CLINICALS
full_story:
Olney Central College’s Massage Therapy Program is accepting appointments for Summer clinicals.

The clinics are open to the public and will be held from 9:15 am to 2 pm on July 11th and July 24th at the Terry L. Bruce West Richland Center in Noble.

Clinics are by appointment only and can be made by calling 618-392-2430.  Callers should leave a message with their names, contact information and dates desired.  Students will return phone messages during Monday and Wednesday evening classes to confirm appointments.

title: MAN IDENTIFIED
full_story:
Illinois State Police have identified the man whose remains were found in Lake Mattoon Sunday evening.

ISP said that boaters saw part of an arm, belonging to 38-year-old Dalewayne Turner of Plainfield, floating in the lake.

The arm had distinct tattoos, including one of a skeleton holding a Green Bay Packers helmet and another of an unknown letter or number.

ISP stated that there is no threat to the public, and no other information is available.

title: IDOT ADVISES DRIVERS TO BE ALERT
full_story:
With extremely high temperatures and humidity impacting the entire state, the Illinois Department of Transportation is cautioning the public to be on the lookout for pavement failures on roads and to stay alert for crews making emergency repairs.

Pavement failures, buckling and blowouts occur with little warning during periods of prolonged heat and humidity, resulting in uneven driving surfaces.  While it’s impossible to predict where or when these failures might occur, maintenance personnel will be monitoring road conditions and on standby to make repairs as quickly as possible when they are observed and reported.

Pavement failures can be reported to IDOT by calling 800-452-4368 or by reaching out to law enforcement via 911.

The public is advised to anticipate slowing traffic and move over for workers and other emergency personnel when repairs are being made.

Additionally, if you are traveling during extreme heat, pack extra water.  Becoming stranded could be dangerous without proper hydration, as dehydration can happen quickly.

For more information about pavement failures and how they occur, take a look at this educational video created by IDOT.

title: BEWARE REPAIR SCAMS
full_story:
As folks in southern Illinois continue to clean up after the recent storms, Attorney General Kwame Raoul is warning residents to be aware of storm-related repair scams.

The Attorney General said scammers are looking to exploit homeowners and business owners who may need repairs after the storms, noting these “storm chasers” use the opportunity to pressure people into making quick and often expensive decisions about cleanup and construction work.

Scam artists may be operating as public adjusters who offer “free” inspections to submit a claim to property owners’ insurance companies.

Home and business owners should check with their local governments for more information about permits or other local requirements before hiring anyone.

You should visit the IDFPR’s website to search for roofing licenses.  You can also visit the DOI’s website or call (866) 445-5364 to verify that a public adjuster is licensed and in good standing.

You can contact the Attorney General’s Consumer Fraud Hotline at 1-800-243-0607 or visit the website to report any suspicious activity.

title: NEW LAWS
full_story:
A new batch of laws officially took effect Wednesday in Illinois, and a few of them are worth knowing about, especially if you’re a senior driver, a parent, or someone who enjoys a cocktail-to-go.

The biggest change for many Central Illinois residents involves older drivers.  Under the new laws, Illinois drivers who are 79 or older will still need to renew their licenses in person at their local Secretary of State’s office or ‘DMV,’ but they will no longer be required to take a driving test to do so.  Going forward, the driving test requirement kicks in for any commercial drivers license holders who are 75 or older, or for any driver who is 87 or older.

Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias announced the change in an effort to make the renewal process simpler for the state’s senior citizens.

For parents and schools, a new expansion of the state’s “cyberbullying” definition goes into effect starting this upcoming school year.  The updated definition now includes the posting or distribution of unauthorized digital images or videos by electronic means.  This measure is said to reflect how bullying has evolved with the current state of social media and smartphones.

On a lighter note, to-go cocktails and adult beverages are now here to stay in Illinois.  This idea became particularly popular at the height of the COVID pandemic.  Now bars and restaurants are allowed to serve cocktails in to-go containers, becoming what is now a permanent law.  As long as you’re 21 or older, Illinois businesses can keep serving you those drinks even as you are on the way out the door.

A couple of other laws also took effect today.  The state’s licensing language for childcare providers is being updated, officially replacing the term “daycare” with “early care and education” in state literature.  And Illinois’ ban on certain animals in traveling circus shows has been expanded beyond elephants to now include non-human primates and large cats such as: lions, tigers, leopards, jaguars, and cougars.
